subject: MedTech pilot: evaluation rollout contingencies & evidence timeline
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@medtechsystems.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medtechsystems.com, ajay.rao@medtechsystems.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot kickoff & procurement checklist — conditional commitment

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the model routing controls. Procurement asked me to consolidate a short list of gating items they need to sign off on a pilot/PO so we can move to an SOW. High level:

- SOC2 evidence matrix (or letter) + list of exported logs available (audit trail).
- A short-term assurance that PHI-related prompts will be redacted or not logged for the pilot.
- Clarification on whether we can run a non-prod on-prem demo for six weeks (air-gapped).
- A simple canary rollback plan if the model behavior drifts on their dataset.

They said if we can provide the SOC2 evidence and a redaction plan by next Thursday (6/3), legal will greenlight the SOW and sign the pilot at the committed price in our proposal.

I've attached the SOW draft and marked the procurement items. Can someone at Redwood confirm what you can commit to and any timing constraints? We're trying to avoid extended security reviews.

Appreciate it,
Claire
Director of Product Operations
MedTech Systems

Attachments: MedTech_SOW_v2.pdf

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot kickoff & procurement checklist — conditional commitment

Folks — forwarding Claire's email (thread above). Key asks: SOC2 evidence, a short-term PII/PHI redaction option for the pilot, possible on-prem non-prod demo, and a canary rollback plan. Procurement needs confirmations by 6/3.

My read and asks for Product/Eng:
- Can we deliver an evidence matrix (existing SOC2 docs + exported log types) by EOD Tue (6/1)? I think Security can package this but need Product help to state what logs are available per-tenant.
- Is there a quick toggle we can offer (deployment/config) to suppress storing prompt inputs for a tenant or run redaction on ingest? If not, what's the minimal engineering work to add a per-tenant "no_input_retention" flag for a pilot?
- For an on-prem non-prod demo: can we provide a pre-baked VM/container image and a simple install playbook for their infra team? If that's heavy, can we offer a controlled VPN demo instead?
- Canary rollback: need Product to sign off on a quick canary plan that operations can run.

This is a $720k ARR mid-enterprise pilot -> full contract if successful. Monica / Ben — can you weigh in on the timeline pressure from procurement? Laura / Connor — can you confirm feasibility?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales (West)
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOC2_evidence_matrix.xlsx (we'll need this populated)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot kickoff & procurement checklist — conditional commitment

Tessa — adding some customer acceptance criteria from CS/PE so Product/Eng have context:

- Pilot success metrics: latency 95p < 220ms, accuracy on their eval set within 4% of baseline.
- Telemetry: they require per-request trace_id/nanosecond timestamp and an auditable action log for admin events.
- Security: must be able to identify which tenant triggered a specific inference and produce a redaction certificate for any PHI-related prompt during the pilot window.

If Product/Eng can implement an input-redaction flow that either (a) strips PHI and returns a redaction token, or (b) opts the tenant into non-retention of inputs (zero retention mode), that's sufficient for procurement. For the on-prem demo: we can support a short-term SSH/VPN access to a preloaded demo cluster — we don't need to ship code. That reduces effort.

I'll coordinate with our Solutions Engineers to provide a runbook and acceptance checklist.

-Monica
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot kickoff & procurement checklist — conditional commitment

Quick read: procurement is firm on the 6/3 ask. We have 1 week. Deal economics: pilot -> production if successful; $720k ARR committed in our proposal; legal will sign on approval. We should treat this as a high-impact priority.

Concrete asks to Product/Eng:
1) Can we ship a minimal "no_input_retention" config toggle scoped to pilot tenant(s) within 5 business days? If yes, what is required (API flag + UI toggle + docs)?
2) If #1 not possible in the window, can we provide a controlled ingestion proxy that strips inputs before they hit our runtime (proxy maintained by SEs for pilot)?
3) SOC2 evidence: Security will assemble, but Product should confirm list of exported logs (request/response bodies, KV cache hits, routing decisions, timestamped traces).

Connor — can you give a quick sanity check on effort for #1 vs #2? If engineering bills time, Sales will justify as deal-cost.

Thanks — Ben
Account Executive

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot kickoff & procurement checklist — conditional commitment

Thanks for the context — here's what Product proposes (tradeoffs included):

Summary (what we can commit by 6/3):
- SOC2 evidence matrix: Security will package the SOC2 artifacts and Product will supply a short export list. ETA: 6/1 EOD. (low risk)
- Canary rollback plan: We can provide an operations playbook for canary deployments and auto-fallback to a baseline model. ETA: 6/2. (low risk)

What requires engineering time and proposed scope/ETA:
1) No-input-retention per-tenant flag (recommended path):
   - Scope: config flag at routing layer to mark requests as "non-retained"; logging writes a redaction token instead of full prompt. Requires changes in routing, telemetry, and small UI exposure.
   - Estimate: 5 dev days + 2 SRE days for validation -> target completion 6/9 (can accelerate if we deprioritize other sprint items).
   - Tradeoffs: faster to implement at routing layer but will not retroactively delete any persisted KV cache artifacts created before the flag.

2) SE-managed proxy (fallback path):
   - Scope: a lightweight ingestion proxy maintained by Solutions Eng that strips or hashes inputs before forwarding. No runtime changes required.
   - Estimate: 2 SE days to build/configure + supporting docs -> target 6/3 if we start today.
   - Tradeoffs: Operational burden on SEs; less elegant but meets procurement timeline.

Recommendation: Commit publicly to the SE-managed proxy for the pilot (meets 6/3), and schedule the per-tenant flag for the sprint starting 6/7 to have a cleaner long-term solution. If Sales agrees, we'll produce the SOC2 export, the canary runbook, and the proxy configuration by 6/3.

Connor — please confirm the SE-engineering handoff and whether the proxy approach introduces any blockers (container images, firewall rules, or certs).

Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console
